column3: recently; in the next few days
column5: The weather has been very cold in recent days.
column6: 近日 is a written word for "in the last few days" or "in the next few days": 近日来 (recently), 近日将 (soon). Use 最近 in speech.

column4: 我们要进一步了解这个问题。
column5: We need to understand this problem further.
column6: 进一步 means "a step further" and goes before a verb: 进一步了解 (to understand further), 进一步提高 (to improve further).

column5: This is a classic film.
column6: 经典 is something of lasting quality: 经典电影 (a classic film), 经典作品 (a classic work). It is also a noun: 这首歌是经典.

column4: 他的精力很好，每天工作十个小时。
column5: He has a lot of energy and works ten hours every day.
column6: 精力 is the mental and physical energy you need for doing things: 精力很好 (full of energy), 没有精力 (to have no energy for it).

column5: He is full of energy today.
column6: 精神 is read jīngshen when it means "lively" or "energy" (有精神, 没精神). When it means "spirit" or "mind" it is read jīngshén (民族精神, 精神压力).

column5: This gift gave him a pleasant surprise.
column6: 惊喜 is a happy surprise: 给……一个惊喜 (to give someone a nice surprise). It is an adjective and a noun.

column5: He runs a small restaurant.
column6: 经营 is to run a business: 经营商店, 经营公司. It is more formal than 开, as in 开店.

column5: The room is very quiet.
column6: 静 means quiet and still: 很静, 安静 (quiet, peaceful). In 静下来 (to quiet down) it is a verb.

column4: 晚上他们去了一家酒吧。
column5: In the evening they went to a bar.
column6: 酒吧 is a bar where people drink and listen to music: 去酒吧, 一家酒吧.

column4: 这是一个很久远的故事。
column5: This is a story from very long ago.
column6: 久远 means far back in time: 年代久远 (from a long time ago), 久远的历史 (a distant past).

column4: 他跳进河里救了一个孩子。
column5: He jumped into the river and saved a child.
column6: 救 is to save someone from danger: 救人 (to save a person), 救命 (to save a life; 救命！ is also a cry for help).

column5: Quickly call an ambulance!
column6: 救护车 is an ambulance. In China the number to call for one is 120.

column4: 现在大学生就业越来越难。
column5: Getting a job is getting harder and harder for university students now.
column6: 就业 is to find work, and also employment: 就业机会 (job opportunities), 帮助就业 (to help people find work). 找工作 is the everyday phrase.

column4: 小区里的居民都很友好。
column5: The residents of the neighbourhood are all friendly.
column6: 居民 is a person who lives in a place: 城市居民 (city residents), 小区居民 (residents of a housing estate).

column4: 他居然忘了自己的生日。
column5: He actually forgot his own birthday.
column6: 居然 shows surprise that something happened or did not: 居然不知道 (to be surprised that someone does not know).

column4: 他在这座城市居住了十年。
column5: He has lived in this city for ten years.
column6: 居住 is a formal word for live: 居住环境 (the living environment), 适合居住 (suitable to live in). In speech people say 住.

column5: I like eating tangerines.
column6: 橘子 is a mandarin orange or tangerine, a sweet fruit that is easy to peel.

column5: According to reports, it will rain heavily tomorrow.
column6: 据 means "according to" and starts a sentence: 据说 (it is said), 据报道 (according to reports), 据朋友说 (according to a friend).

column3: to be apart from; distance from
column5: This place is not far from the railway station.
column6: 距 means "to be apart from" and is written: 距离 (distance), 距……不远 (not far from …), 距考试 (until the exam).

column3: to have; to possess (the needed conditions)
column4: 他具备这个工作需要的条件。
column5: He has the conditions this job needs.
column6: 具备 is to have the needed qualities or conditions: 具备条件 (to meet the conditions), 具备能力 (to have the ability).

column3: theatre (the hall where shows are on)
column5: We go to the theatre to watch a performance.
column6: 剧场 is a theatre building where plays and shows are put on. A cinema is 电影院.

column4: 这个城市发生了巨大的变化。
column5: This city has undergone huge changes.
column6: 巨大 is huge, bigger than 大: 巨大的变化, 巨大的压力 (huge pressure), 巨大的成功 (a huge success).

column5: It is said that the food at this restaurant is delicious.
column6: 据说 means "it is said". It tells what you heard from others, not what you saw yourself.

column5: Please be more specific.
column6: 具体 means specific and detailed: 具体时间 (the exact time), 具体情况 (the specific situation).

column4: 这个办法具有很多好处。
column5: This method has many benefits.
column6: 具有 is a formal "to have", used for qualities and features: 具有特点 (to have features), 具有价值 (to have value).

column5: He donated some money to the school.
column6: 捐 is to give money or things for a good cause: 捐钱 (to donate money), 捐书 (to donate books).

column5: I absolutely trust him.
column6: 绝对 means absolutely: 绝对不会 (absolutely will not), 绝对正确 (absolutely correct). As an adjective it means "absolute".

column5: They have reached the final.
column6: 决赛 is the final match: 进入决赛 (to reach the final), 决赛 is the last round of a competition.

column4: 他在电影里演一个重要的角色。
column5: He plays an important role in the film.
column6: 角色 is a part played by an actor or a person in a group: 演角色 (to play a role), 重要角色 (an important role).

column5: He has made up his mind to learn Chinese well.
column6: 决心 is strong determination: 下决心 (to make up one's mind), 有决心 (to be determined). It is also a verb: 决心学习.

column4: 这家公司在开发新软件。
column5: This company is developing new software.
column6: 开发 is to develop resources, land or products: 开发新产品 (to develop new products). 发展 is to grow; 开发 is to start something new.

column3: to be open; to open up
column5: The park opens at six in the morning.
column6: 开放 means to be open to the public (公园开放) and to open up (改革开放, reform and opening up). As an adjective it describes an open mind: 很开放.

column5: The competition opens tomorrow.
column6: 开幕 is when a big event or show begins: 开幕式 (the opening ceremony). The opposite is 闭幕 (to close).

column4: 我们去看了运动会的开幕式。
column5: We went to see the opening ceremony of the sports meeting.
column6: 开幕式 is the opening ceremony: 参加开幕式 (to attend the opening ceremony).

column5: Please give me a glass of boiled water.
column6: 开水 is water that has been boiled and is drunk hot in China: 喝开水, 一杯开水.

column5: The metro line opens next month.
column6: 开通 is to open a road, a line or a service so that people can use it: 开通地铁 (to open a metro line), 开通网络 (to activate internet service).

column5: The new shop opens tomorrow.
column6: 开业 is to start doing business: 正式开业 (officially open), 开业那天 (on the opening day).

column5: The school has launched many activities.
column6: 开展 is to start and carry out an activity on a large scale: 开展活动 (to hold activities), 开展工作 (to carry out work).

column5: I am going to the hospital to visit a friend.
column6: 看望 is to visit someone to see how they are, often someone who is ill or older: 看望老人, 看望病人 (to visit a patient). 参观 is to visit a place.

column4: 他把我看作自己的朋友。
column5: He regards me as his own friend.
column6: 看作 is to think of something as something else: 把 A 看作 B (to regard A as B). It is close to 当作.

column3: to lean on; to depend on
column5: He leans against the door and rests.
column6: 靠 means "to lean on" (靠在墙上), "to depend on" (靠自己) and "to be close to" (靠右边, on the right side).

column5: Do not go near that dog.
column6: 靠近 is to get close to something: 靠近窗户 (near the window), 慢慢靠近 (to approach slowly).

column3: measure word for small round things
column4: 天上有一颗很亮的星星。
column5: There is a very bright star in the sky.
column6: 颗 counts small round things: 一颗星星 (a star), 一颗糖 (a sweet), 一颗牙 (a tooth), 一颗心 (a heart).

column5: He does scientific research at a university.
column6: 科研 is short for 科学研究: 科研人员 (researchers), 科研工作 (research work).

column3: so it is clear that; it shows
column4: 他每天练习，可见他很努力。
column5: He practises every day, which shows he works hard.
column6: 可见 introduces a conclusion drawn from what was just said: ……，可见…… It comes after the reason.

column5: He is a reliable person.
column6: 可靠 means you can depend on it: 可靠的朋友 (a reliable friend), 消息可靠 (the news is reliable).

column5: This film is too scary.
column6: 可怕 is frightening or terrible: 可怕的事, 很可怕. 怕 describes your own fear; 可怕 describes the thing that causes it.

column5: He overcame many difficulties.
column6: 克服 is to overcome a difficulty, a fault or a bad habit: 克服困难 (to overcome difficulties), 克服缺点 (to overcome a fault).

column4: 有问题可以打电话给客服。
column5: If you have a problem, you can call customer service.
column6: 客服 is short for 客户服务: 客服电话 (the customer service number), 在线客服 (online support).

column4: 他对这件事的看法很客观。
column5: His view on this matter is very objective.
column6: 客观 means looking at the facts as they are, not through feelings: 客观地说 (objectively speaking), 客观原因 (an objective cause).

column4: 他今天要见一个重要的客户。
column5: He has to meet an important client today.
column6: 客户 is a person or company that buys from you: 重要客户 (an important client). 顾客 is a shopper in a shop.

column5: The space in this room is very large.
column6: 空间 is the room that is available: 有空间 (to have room), 空间不够 (not enough space). In science it also means space, as opposed to time.

column5: Birds fly in the air.
column6: 空中 is the air or sky above you: 空中飞行 (to fly in the air). It is a place word like 地上 (on the ground).

column4: 他不能控制自己的脾气。
column5: He cannot control his temper.
column6: 控制 is to keep something under your control: 控制时间, 控制自己 (to control oneself), 控制价格 (to control prices).

column5: He puts his money in his pocket.
column6: 口袋 is a pocket or a small bag: 衣服口袋 (a clothes pocket), 裤子口袋 (a trouser pocket).

column4: 每个人的口味都不一样。
column5: Everyone's taste is different.
column6: 口味 is the kind of flavour a person likes: 口味重 (likes strong flavours), 新口味 (a new flavour).

column5: He drove the car into the garage.
column6: 库 is a place for storing things. It is mostly used in words: 车库 (garage), 水库 (reservoir).

column5: This road is very wide.
column6: 宽 means wide: 很宽, 宽的路. For clothes it means loose: 衣服太宽了 (the clothes are too loose).

column4: 这条马路的宽度是二十米。
column5: The width of this road is twenty metres.
column6: 宽度 is how wide something is: 路的宽度. Others in the family are 高度 (height) and 厚度 (thickness).

column3: to lose money; to be at a loss
column4: 这个店今年亏了很多钱。
column5: This shop lost a lot of money this year.
column6: 亏 means "to lose money" (亏钱, 做生意亏了). In 多亏 it means "thanks to": 多亏了你 (thanks to you).

column5: There are many insects in summer.
column6: 昆虫 is an insect. In speech people also say 虫子 (bug). 蝴蝶 (butterfly) is an insect.

column5: The company wants to expand its business.
column6: 扩大 is to make something bigger in size or range: 扩大范围 (to widen the scope), 扩大市场 (to expand the market).

column4: 这个消息的来源是什么？
column5: What is the source of this news?
column6: 来源 is where something comes from: 消息来源 (the source of news), 收入来源 (a source of income), 来源不清楚 (the source is unclear).

column5: He likes physical work.
column6: 劳动 is physical or manual work: 参加劳动 (to take part in labour), 劳动节 (Labour Day, 1 May). 工作 is a job; 劳动 is the work of the body.

column4: 老百姓都希望过上好日子。
column5: Ordinary people all hope for a good life.
column6: 老百姓 means ordinary people, as opposed to officials or leaders: 普通老百姓. It is a warm, everyday word.

column5: His boss is very young.
column6: 老板 is the owner or boss: 饭馆老板 (a restaurant owner). Customers also call a shopkeeper 老板.

column5: My husband is not at home today.
column6: 老公 is a casual word for husband, used by wives. A more formal word is 丈夫.

column5: My maternal grandmother lives in the north.
column6: 姥姥 is your mother's mother, used in the north of China. In the south people say 外婆. 奶奶 is your father's mother.

column5: His wife is very beautiful.
column6: 老婆 is a casual word for wife, used by husbands. A more formal word is 妻子.

column4: 我姥爷每天早上去公园锻炼。
column5: My maternal grandfather goes to the park to exercise every morning.
column6: 姥爷 is your mother's father, used in the north of China. In the south people say 外公. 爷爷 is your father's father.

column5: She is very optimistic about life.
column6: 乐观 is seeing things on the bright side: 乐观的人 (an optimist), 对……很乐观 (to be optimistic about …).

column5: Reading brings a lot of enjoyment.
column6: 乐趣 is the enjoyment you get from doing something: 有乐趣 (to be fun), 找到乐趣 (to find joy in it).

column5: There are tears in her eyes.
column6: 泪 is a tear. It is mostly used in words: 眼泪 (tears), 流泪 (to shed tears), 泪水.

column5: These two kinds of books are both very interesting.
column6: 类 is a kind or category: 这类 (this kind), 分类 (to sort into categories). As a measure word it counts kinds: 两类人.

column5: Her face is covered in tears.
column6: 泪水 is tears as a mass, a little more literary than 眼泪: 泪水流下来 (tears fall).

column5: These two things are very similar.
column6: 类似 means similar: 类似的问题 (a similar problem), 类似于 (to be similar to). It is a verb and an adjective.
